THE ARTIFACT SPLIT INVERTS THE `real` RANKING, confirming claim.law.MV_regnorm-census-ranks-tractability-and-real-actively-misranks-it.20260901.v1 on a fresh roster. ResolveWorldData carries the largest `real` in the TU by a factor of two (1518) yet has only 12 genuine rows against 661 renaming rows; fn_8005D730 shows 98 STRUCTURAL rows of which 93 are pure artifacts of ONE missing instruction. Ranking this roster by `real` would have sent the session to the two worst-conditioned functions first.

THREE FUNCTIONS NEEDED NO WORK OR NO FURTHER WORK, established read-only:
(1) fn_8005ACE0 carries gate `real 10` but `fndiff --clean` reports 'MATCH (pool-name noise only), 0 real diff lines (+36 pool-name lines suppressed)'. Its regnorm verdict is EXACT. The gate's non-zero real is pool-label noise; the function is done and must not be worked.
(2) LoadWorldData's cap (attempt.gw-loadworlddata-residual-is-solely-the-pclass-copy.20260901.v1) is INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by this census: 0 genuine structural rows, all 5 branch rows artifacts, and the 7 unpaired rows are exactly the addi/mr home-copy event that record names. Zero probes were spent re-testing it.
(3) fn_8005FDA8's anonymous-pool relocations are a benign splitter artifact, not a defect - see attempt.GW_fn8005fda8-pool-label-artifact-not-a-wrong-symbol-defect.20260901.v1.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTANCE OF THE BENIGN RELOCATION-NAMING ARTIFACT, NOW ON JUMP TABLES. fn_8005D730 rows @0x58/@0x5c and @0x4e4/@0x4e8 show target `jumptable_8011CAD4` / `jumptable_8011CA9C` against our `@2725` / `@2727`. Same mechanism as the .sdata2 pool labels: both sides emit their own compiler-generated switch table and only the splitter-invented name differs. FOUR of that function's five genuine rows are this artifact. GENERAL RULE for this TU and any NonMatching TU: an anonymous-vs-named relocation row is a DEFECT only when the target symbol is a real named object with non-pool referents; it is an ARTIFACT when the target symbol is a splitter-invented `lbl_`/`jumptable_` over compiler-generated data. Check the DATA at the address, never the name shape.

QUEUED FOR THE NEXT LANE - a frame/saved-register census run across the whole roster from the same regnorm dumps, three live leads not worked this session:
(a) fn_8005F0F4: target `stmw r25,220(r1)`, ours `stmw r25,228(r1)`. Same saved set (r25-r31), but OUR FRAME IS 8 BYTES LARGER (256 vs 248). This is the OPPOSITE polarity from the fn_80060114 pad that succeeded this session - here 8 bytes of over-declared local must come OUT. Cheap to test and nobody has.
(b) fn_8005C1DC: target `stmw r23,100(r1)`, ours `stmw r22,96(r1)`. Frame agrees at 136; we SAVE ONE EXTRA callee-saved register (r22). A register-pressure lead, not a pad lead.
(c) fn_80062A00: ours is 8 bytes larger AND saves an extra register (target r22-r31 / ours r21-r31). NOTE the +8 frame axis is already VETOED as an inline-expansion question by attempt.fn-80062a00-inline-frame-screen.20260831.v1 - the EXTRA SAVED REGISTER is the part that screen did not cover.

THE HOME-COPY SHAPE IS THE TU'S DOMINANT SINGLE-INSTRUCTION RESIDUAL: it appears at fn_8005D730 +0xb0, fn_80060114 +0x28 and (in the opposite, ours-has-the-extra-copy polarity) LoadWorldData. Two of the three are the unserved inverse direction of claim.law.DC_copy-form-class-is-directional-and-its-inverse-population-is-unserved.20260901.v1. One instance of the inverse direction WAS closed at source this session (fn_8005E90C) and the lever and its boundary are recorded as claim.law.GW_block-scope-splits-a-coalesced-copy-but-a-same-scope-copy-folds.20260901.v1 - screen that law's scope-and-join discriminator before spending probes on the remaining two.
